events.title: Paul Revere's Midnight Ride
events.description: On the night of April 18, 1775, Paul Revere and William Dawes rode from Boston to Lexington to warn colonial leaders John Hancock and Samuel Adams that British troops were marching to arrest them and seize militia supplies at Concord.
events.significance: The ride preceded the battles of Lexington and Concord on April 19, which began the American Revolutionary War and was later immortalized in Longfellow's poem.

events.title: San Francisco Earthquake
events.description: At 5:12 a.m., a magnitude 7.9 earthquake struck San Francisco, California, and the fires that followed destroyed about 80 percent of the city. Roughly 3,000 people are estimated to have died and more than half the population was left homeless.
events.significance: One of the deadliest and most destructive natural disasters in US history, it led to major advances in seismology, earthquake-resistant building codes, and urban fire safety.

events.title: Death of Albert Einstein
events.description: Albert Einstein, the German-born theoretical physicist who developed the theory of relativity, died at age 76 at Princeton Hospital in New Jersey after an abdominal aortic aneurysm ruptured.
events.significance: Einstein's work reshaped modern physics, including our understanding of space, time, gravity, and energy, and he remains a lasting symbol of scientific genius.

events.title: Independence of Zimbabwe
events.description: Southern Rhodesia became the independent Republic of Zimbabwe after years of armed struggle and the Lancaster House Agreement. Canaan Banana became ceremonial president and Robert Mugabe became prime minister.
events.significance: It ended British colonial rule and white-minority governance in the territory, marking a major milestone in the decolonization of Africa.

events.title: League of Nations Dissolved
events.description: The League of Nations, the international organization founded after World War I, held its final assembly in Geneva and voted to dissolve itself, transferring its remaining assets and responsibilities to the United Nations.
events.significance: The League's dissolution formally closed the first major experiment in collective security and cleared the way for the UN to become the central body of international cooperation.
